summary: Feed s108_single is degraded: NDR requires bidirectional traffic but 22.9% of TCP sessions (24/105) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. Other checks (duplicates, drops, overload, VLAN, encryption) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is delivering only one direction for ~23% of sessions. Most likely cause is single-sided TAP/SPAN or asymmetric routing where forward and reverse paths are not both aggregated to this NDR port, or broker hashing is splitting directions across different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions for stateful TCP reassembly and detection. With 22.9% one-way sessions it cannot reconstruct flows, misses handshakes, C2, lateral movement and exfiltration, causing false negatives and incomplete incident timeline.

recommended_fix.why: NDR requires both directions on same tool port for session reconstruction. Aggregating forward+reverse with symmetric hashing ensures complete flows reach this NDR and restores detection coverage.
